Under the Defense & Geopolitical Fragmentation megatrend, here are the real European (non-US) names — I filtered out the US primes (Lockheed/LOM, Raytheon/5UR, Boeing, GE, Palantir) that show up only because they're cross-listed on XETRA/LSE.

Core European defense primes & leaders:
• Rheinmetall (RHM.XETRA, DE) — the standout European land-systems/ammo leader
• BAE Systems (BA.LSE, GB) — UK prime
• Airbus (AIR.PA / AIR.XETRA, NL/EU) — defense & aerospace prime
• Thales (HO.PA, FR) — electronics/systems prime
• Leonardo (0ONG.LSE, IT) — Italian prime
• Saab (0GWL.LSE, SE) — Swedish defense-electronics leader
• Dassault Aviation (AM.PA, FR) — combat aircraft
• Safran (SAF.PA, FR) — propulsion/defense electronics
• Rolls-Royce (RR.LSE, GB) — propulsion/naval
• Kongsberg Gruppen (0F08.LSE, NO) — Norwegian missiles/maritime

Naval / land / munitions & sensors: Hensoldt (HAG.XETRA, DE, sensors), TKMS + thyssenkrupp + Renk (DE, naval/drivetrain), Fincantieri (1F80.XETRA, IT, shipbuilding), Babcock & QinetiQ (BAB.LSE / QQ.LSE, GB), Chemring (CHG.LSE, GB, energetics), Smiths Group (SMIN.LSE, GB), Exail (EXA.PA, FR, naval), H&K (MLHK.PA, DE, small arms), Indra (0HA9.LSE, ES). These are all genuine European arms/aerospace names — no US primes in the list.
